segments.oily: Reviewers with oily or combination-oily skin report reduced oil, smaller-looking pores, and fewer breakouts with no added greasiness.
segments.dry: Reviewers describing dry skin generally tolerate the product well, though a few note increased dryness or flaking with frequent use, prompting them to space out applications.
segments.combination: Combination-skin reviewers report smoother texture and fewer hormonal or acne breakouts without irritation.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers form the largest single group and mostly describe little to no irritation compared with retinol or tretinoin, though a minority report burning, itching, or breakouts severe enough to stop use.
segments.mature: Reviewers in their 40s-70s report visible improvement in fine lines, firmness, and dullness, generally without irritation, and see it as a gentler alternative to prescription retinoids.

concerns.aging: Reviewers report diminished fine lines, improved firmness, and a brighter, more even look, some after only a few weeks; several mature reviewers explicitly credit it with visible anti-aging results with no irritation.
concerns.dehydration: Some reviewers note the product is hydrating or non-drying relative to other retinoids, while others (including one with reactive, dehydrated skin) report dryness or flaking that requires reduced frequency.
concerns.redness: Several reviewers say it reduced redness or caused none at all, but a few reviewers explicitly report redness or a burning/stinging sensation after use, and one asks for a lower-redness formula.
concerns.barrier: Reviewers coming from tretinoin or strong retinol describe the product as easier on the barrier with less peeling and irritation, though one reviewer with a reactive barrier still reports it as too strong initially.
concerns.spots: Reviewers report fading of dark spots, hyperpigmentation, and post-acne discoloration with continued use over several weeks.
concerns.blemishes: Most reviewers with acne-prone skin report fewer breakouts, faster healing of blemishes, and reduced closed comedones over weeks of use; however, a few reviewers report a breakout, purge, or cystic-type reaction after only one or two uses.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers with oily skin report the product controls oil and leaves a lightweight, non-greasy finish.

extraits.titre: So good! Need a 0.1% retinal strength to step up!
extraits.texte: I am in love with this gel lotion hybrid! It works so well without any irritation. My rosacea prone skin is absolutely in love with the formulation. However, please come with a 0.1% retinaldehyde for those who want to step up their retinoid game with this amazing formulation.

extraits.titre: An affordable, less irritating Retin-A alternative
extraits.texte: It's fantastic to have an opportunity to enjoy the benefits of Retin-A without the irritation for my sensitive, mature skin. That is why I decided to purchase this product and I have to say that this formulation is working. I am getting some peeling and flaking without redness or burning and the dullness is gone. My skin looks fresher and glowing. I will continue to purchase this.

I have reactive and dehydrated skin and I have tried to incorporate a retinal into my routine the last three years. I have not found something that doesnt aggravate and ruin my barrier at some point. I can use this right after applying my essence and my skin is totally in tact the next day. No burning, redness, or sensitivity. The texture is wonderful and I love that there is no overpowering smell. I have been using this about three weeks so I cannot say anything about longer term use, but I have noticed myskin becoming more even toned. Super happy that I made this purchase and the product has exceeded my hopes.

i have acne prone skin, oily and redness.. and i this product so much.. this retinal control my oil, reduce my redness, pore look smaller and my acne gone....thank you naturium you make amazing product.. love love...

I wanted a retinaldehyde because it's supposed to be one of the stronger otc options for a retinoid- I started with adapaline, then retinol, and still not having achieved what I was looking for wanted to step it up. But I found this to be less potent than adapalene gel. It's a nice formula, pretty hydrating as far as retinoids go, layers well with other products and doesn't cause any pilling, and I enjoy the yellow color of the product for easy even application purposes. It's would be great for a beginner. But something in the formula is killing the potency that retinaldehyde promises.
